MultiEdit.name: MultiEdit
MultiEdit.description:
Performs multiple exact string replacements in a single file in one atomic operation. This is more efficient than multiple Edit calls when making several changes to the same file.

Usage:
- Read the file before editing so old_string matches the current text.
- Edits are applied sequentially in the order provided, so later edits see the result of earlier ones.
- Each edit's old_string must be unique in the file (after prior edits are applied).
- Prefer this tool over multiple Edit calls when making 2+ changes to the same file - it reduces round trips and ensures atomicity.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

edits.description: Array of edit operations to apply sequentially. Each edit's old_string must be unique in the file (after prior edits are applied).

new_string.description: The text to replace it with.

annotate_recording.name: annotate_recording
annotate_recording.description: Add a structured annotation to the active recording at the current timestamp. The video will slow down around annotation points.

test.description: Test name in 'It should ...' style. Required for test_start and assertion.

test_result.description: Whether the assertion passed, failed, or was untested. Required for assertion type.

assertion.description: Concise description of what was checked. Required for assertion type.

description.description: Description of the setup step. Required for setup type.

apply_patch.name: apply_patch
apply_patch.description: Use the apply_patch tool to edit files. You must include a header with your intended action (Add/Update/Delete). You must prefix new lines with `+` even when creating a new file. To delete a file, use a `*** Delete File: <path>` header with no body. To rename or move a file, add a `*** Move to: <new path>` line immediately after its `*** Update File: <path>` header (you may also include edits in the same hunk). Paths must stay inside the configured workspace. Both `*** Begin Patch` format and standard unified diffs are accepted through the existing patch input.

browser_console.name: browser_console
browser_console.description: View the browser console outputs and optionally run JavaScript. Useful for inspecting errors and debugging when combined with console.log statements in your code. If no code to run is provided, this will just return the recent console output. Requires a connected browser in the sandbox.

content.description: JavaScript code to run in the console. Leave empty to just return the recent console output.

browser_preview.name: browser_preview
browser_preview.description:
Show the user a live browser preview of a web app or page running in the sandbox — something they will open and use, not a document they will read. If the deliverable is a report, guide, analysis, write-up, or self-contained HTML/PDF, attach the file with `message_user` instead of starting a static file server. A preview depends on the running sandbox; an attachment is durable when configured storage is available.

Provide a short human-readable `name`, local `ports` with the user-facing port first, and optionally an app-relative `path` including a query string. Pass all required ports for multi-service apps. Call this after starting a dev server that the user should open, and call it again after restarting the server if the sandbox expires. A configured authenticated preview backend is required. Do not describe a preview as a public deployment or claim it survives sandbox expiry.

name.description: Short human-readable label for this preview (e.g. "Bun app preview").

ports.description: Local ports the app is served on. At least one is required. Include both the frontend and backend ports when the app has both.

path.description: App-relative path to open on the first port, optionally including a query string.

computer.name: computer
computer.description: Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with the sandbox desktop GUI. This tool does not execute shell commands; use `exec` for terminal operations. Actions include `key`, `type`, `cursor_position`, `mouse_move`, clicks, drag, `scroll`, `left_mouse_down`, `left_mouse_up`, `hold_key`, `wait`, `zoom`, `screenshot`, and `read_dom`. Coordinates use the sandbox display space; do not assume a fixed screen resolution. You can perform multiple consecutive actions in one call by providing multiple entries in the `actions` array. `read_dom` reads the connected browser DOM when available; screenshots require an available computer backend. Inspect the result before claiming that an action took effect.

actions.description: A list of actions to perform sequentially.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge of the screen) and y (pixels from the top edge of the screen) coordinates to move the cursor to. Required for mouse_move and left_click_drag. Optional for click actions (if not provided, clicks at current position).

start_coordinate.description: (x, y): The starting x and y coordinates for left_click_drag action.

text.description: Required for type and key actions. For type, the text to type. For key, a key or key combination to press (e.g., 'Return', 'ctrl+c', 'alt+Tab'). Also used for hold_key to specify which key to hold, and optionally for scroll to specify a modifier key.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for scroll action.

scroll_amount.description: The number of 'clicks' to scroll. Required for scroll action.

duration.description: The duration in seconds. Required for hold_key and wait actions.

key.description: Optional modifier key to hold while performing a click action (e.g., 'ctrl', 'shift', 'alt').

region.description: [x1, y1, x2, y2]: The coordinates defining the region to zoom into. Required for zoom action.

deploy.name: deploy
deploy.description: Deploy a project only through the configured sandbox preview backend. Supported commands are `frontend` (run `npm run dev`), `backend` (run `npm start`), `expose` (preview an already listening HTTP port), and `logs` (read a deployment record). The directory must stay inside the workspace; a backend volume requires a preconfigured sandbox volume. These deployments are temporary authenticated previews, not publicly hosted sites. Do not claim a permanent public URL, approval card, Fly.io or static hosting. Get explicit user approval before making an app publicly reachable through any separate publishing workflow; never treat this preview as that approval.

dir.description: Project directory on the box to deploy. Required for 'frontend' and 'backend'.

volume.description: Whether to attach a persistent volume (backend only).

port.description: Local port number to expose to the internet (required for 'expose').

describe_image.name: describe_image
describe_image.description: Describe the contents of an image file on the box, or ask a specific question about it. Provide the path to an image (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, etc.) and optionally a question. Without a question you get a detailed natural-language description including any visible text. With a question the model answers that question about the image. Useful for inspecting screenshots, diagrams, or other images you cannot otherwise read.

image_path.description: Path to the image file on the remote box.

question.description: Optional question to ask about the image. When provided, the vision model will answer this specific question instead of producing a generic description.

opulent_automation_manage.name: opulent_automation_manage
opulent_automation_manage.description: Manage Opulent automations stored in this runtime. Supported triggers are recurring schedules, GitHub push/pull-request, Slack message, and incoming webhook; actions include starting a session or scan, scanning new commits, messaging a session, and triage. Call action="schemas" before building one to see supported types; `validate_create` and `validate_update` dry-run without mutation. For updates, fetch with `get` and include fields you intend to keep rather than assuming hosted per-organization merge semantics. Repository scope is enforced locally. Tool grants, identity/network policy, preflight scripts, notifications, ACU metering, and hosted webapp URLs require separate providers and are rejected here. Never imply a listed trigger is connected to a live external event without verifying ingestion.

host.description: Host value retained in the schema; the local scan action uses allowlisted repository names and does not select an organization-default Git host.

AutomationConcurrencySpec.description: Concurrency limits for an automation's runs.

max_concurrent_runs.description: Maximum in-flight runs; further triggered events wait in the automation's queue. A run frees its slot once its session finishes and is awaiting further instructions, not only when the session stops. Omitted/null = unlimited.

max_queue_depth.description: Maximum triggered events waiting in the queue; events beyond this are dropped (0 = never queue). Requires max_concurrent_runs. Omitted/null = unlimited.

AutomationConditionGroupSpec.description: AND-group: every condition in the group must match.

AutomationConditionSpec.description: A single field/operator/value filter on the triggering event.

field.description: Event field used by local conditions. Call action="schemas" for supported triggers and operators. Slack channel conditions use the channel ID, not a name or #handle.

operator.description: Comparison operator; the operators each field supports come from action="schemas".

value.description: Comparison value; its type follows the operator (string/number/bool for eq/neq, string for contains/matches, [low, high] numbers for between, string list for in/not_in/globs, RRULE string for recurrence, omitted for is_empty/is_not_empty).

AutomationConditionsSpec.description: Event filter: OR of AND-groups (fixed two-level DNF).

AutomationEmailNotificationSpec.description: Email ping about the automation's dispatch outcomes.

when.description: Which dispatch outcomes trigger the email.

recipients.description: Unsupported notification recipients. The local automation handler rejects notifications and does not email the creator.

AutomationInvocationLimitsSpec.description: Rate limit on the automation's own firing.

max_per_window.description: Maximum trigger firings per rolling window.

window_seconds.description: Length of the rolling window in seconds.

AutomationIpv4DestinationSpec.description: Allowed IPv4 address or CIDR block.

AutomationIpv6DestinationSpec.description: Allowed IPv6 address or CIDR block.

max_acu_limit.description: Unsupported ACU limit: the local handler rejects max_acu_limit without a metering backend.

invocations.description: Rate-limits the automation's own firing. Omitted/null = unlimited.

AutomationMessageSessionActionSpec.description: Messages an existing Opulent session per triggering event.

target_opulent_id.description: Existing local session ID to message. The session must exist in this runtime; auto_create may create and remember a local target on the first event.

prompt.description: The triggering event's payload is appended automatically. Required when creating or adding this action; on a merge-semantics update, omit it to keep the stored value (null is invalid).

auto_create.description: When true, the first trigger creates a new long-running session owned by the automation and subsequent triggers message it.

AutomationNetPolicySpec.description: Unsupported per-automation network-policy configuration. The handler rejects session_settings and security_profile.

allow.description: Destinations spawned sessions may reach; everything else is blocked.

AutomationNotificationsSpec.description: Unsupported dispatch notifications. The local automation handler rejects notifications.

AutomationPreflightSpec.description: Unsupported in this runtime. Preflight scripts, event/state/output files and fan-out checks require an installed execution backend; automation creation rejects preflight.

source.description: Unsupported preflight script source. This runtime does not resolve file:// URIs or run preflight scripts.

timeout_seconds.description: Unsupported preflight timeout; no script is run by this runtime.

secret_names.description: Unsupported preflight secret grants. Do not include secret values or assume environment access.

enabled.description: Unsupported preflight enable flag; preflight is not installed by this runtime.

AutomationReplySpec.description: Where the trigger's spawned session binds and its response is delivered.

type.description: notify_thread: one-way 'session started' breadcrumb in the triggering Slack thread; attach_thread: two-way binding to the triggering Slack thread (both Slack triggers only, and they can't be combined); post_response: deliver the agent's response to the triggering context.

AutomationRunAsSpec.description: Identity that triggered sessions run as and are attributed to.

type.description: Unsupported automation run identity. The handler rejects run_as instead of switching organization or creator identity.

AutomationScanNewCommitsActionSpec.description: Re-scan an existing local code scan after its last completed run with a validated head SHA when the automation fires. This starts a local child run; do not infer hosted organization entitlement or a scan-runs UI.

scan_id.description: Existing local scan ID to extend. The scan must have a completed run with a validated head SHA, or the automation action fails; find it with opulent_code_scan_manage action="list_scans".

AutomationSessionConfigSpec.description:
Config for the session a start_session action spawns.

``repos`` and ``playbook_id`` are read-only (derived from prompt tokens);
reference repos and playbooks inline in the prompt instead of passing
them here.

tags.description: Session tags are retained in this schema but not applied to spawned sessions by the local automation dispatcher.

platform.description: Platform setting is retained in this schema but not used for local spawned-session VM placement.

bypass_approval.description: Auto-approves child-session creation (the only check this flag bypasses).

AutomationSessionNotificationsSpec.description: Where the spawned session's content goes (currently Slack only).

slack.description: Can't be combined with notify_thread/attach_thread trigger replies, and post_response mode can't be combined with a post_response trigger reply.

AutomationSessionSettingsSpec.description: Settings applied to every session the automation spawns.

opulent_mode.description: Unsupported per-automation session setting. The handler rejects session_settings; it does not select an organization mode.

net_policy.description: Unsupported per-automation network policy. The handler rejects session_settings; no null value grants unrestricted access.

AutomationSessionSlackSpec.description: Gives the spawned session a Slack home in the given channel.

mode.description: Slack notification mode is retained in this schema but not executed by the local automation dispatcher. Do not promise posted replies.

channel_id.description: Required. Slack channel ID (e.g. C0123ABC456), not the channel name or #handle. Must be real and accessible to both the user and the bot; never invent one.

source_channel_id.description: Slack channel ID to watch (e.g. C0123ABC456), not the channel name or #handle.

AutomationSlackChannelSpec.description: Slack channel the spawned sessions' Slack tools may post to.

AutomationSlackNotificationSpec.description: Slack ping about the automation's dispatch outcomes.

when.description: Which dispatch outcomes trigger the Slack message.

channel_id.description: Slack channel ID to post to (e.g. C0123ABC456).

AutomationStartCodeScanActionSpec.description: Start a local code scan when the automation fires. Scans can be expensive: only configure recurring or event-driven scanning on an explicit user request. The local run creates an investigation session; hosted code-scanning entitlements and scan pages are not provided.

scan_mode.description: 'single' (default): one scan of repo_name. 'multi': one combined scan spanning repos.

repo_name.description: Repository to scan (owner/name). Required in single mode.

host.description: Git host of repo_name, when not the org default.

repos.description: Repositories covered by the one scan. Required (non-empty) in multi mode.

profile_id.description: Local scan profile ID defining the objective; use opulent_code_scan_manage action="list_profiles". Non-security scans require a matching profile.

scan_type.description: Scan type, e.g. 'security' (default), 'code-quality', 'performance', 'general'. Must match the chosen profile's scan type.

code_scan_effort.description: Accepted in this schema but not used by the local scan worker; do not promise UI effort or billing semantics.

interactive.description: When true, the scan pauses for user input instead of running unattended.

AutomationStartSessionActionSpec.description: Starts a new Opulent session per triggering event.

prompt.description: Plain-text prompt for a new local session. The event payload is appended by the dispatcher. Pass literal text; inline repository, path, playbook, skill or secret-reference tokens are not expanded by this handler.

AutomationToolsSpec.description: Tool grants for the sessions the automation spawns.

mcp_servers.description: Unsupported per-automation MCP grants. The handler rejects tools; configure and approve providers separately before using MCP tools.

slack_channels.description: Unsupported Slack channel grants. The local automation handler rejects tools; do not promise bot channel access or wildcard public-channel permission.

slack_dm_scope.description: Unsupported per-automation Slack DM grants. The handler rejects tools; do not promise automatic DM delivery.

AutomationTriageSessionActionSpec.description:
Auto-triage: watches a Slack channel, groups each message into tracked
issues, and spawns an investigation session for genuinely new ones. Use it
only to triage a channel's bugs, alerts, or support requests; if every
message is handled the same way (echo, forward, summarize), use start_session
with a slack:message trigger instead, even if the request says 'triage'.
Optional extra condition filters on its slack:message trigger.

setup_prompt.description: How to triage the channel: what counts as an issue, how to investigate, and where to route findings. Required when creating or adding this action; on a merge-semantics update, omit it to keep the stored value (null is invalid).

slack_triage_config.description: Requires exactly one slack:message trigger on the same channel. Required when creating or adding this action; on a merge-semantics update, omit it to keep the stored value (null is invalid).

AutomationTriggerSpec.description: An event that dispatches the automation.

event_type.description: Trigger event type. Call action="schemas" for the fixed local supported set; a configured trigger does not prove an external provider is connected.

conditions.description: Omit (or pass null) to match every event.

replies.description: Reply configuration is not executed by the local dispatcher; do not promise automatic GitHub or Slack responses.

action.description: Supported local actions: list, get, schemas, templates (returns an empty list), create, validate_create, update, validate_update, delete, run. Validation is a dry run. Preflight actions remain in the enum for interface compatibility but the handler rejects them; no script is executed.

automation_id.description: The automation ID. Required for 'get', 'update', 'validate_update', 'delete', and 'run'.

name.description: Human-readable name for the automation (1-500 characters). Required for 'create' and 'validate_create'.

triggers.description:
Events that dispatch the automation. Required for 'create'; replaces all existing triggers when passed to 'update'. Schedule triggers use an RRULE condition (RFC 5545) with the 'recurrence' operator. When the user specifies a timezone, preserve it with an IANA TZID DTSTART and keep BYHOUR/BYMINUTE as the requested local wall-clock values, e.g. {'event_type': 'schedule:recurring', 'conditions': {'any': [{'all': [{'field': 'rrule', 'operator': 'recurrence', 'value': 'DTSTART;TZID=America/Los_Angeles:19700101T000000
RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=6;BYMINUTE=0'}]}]}}. DST follows that timezone. Only use a timezone-less or UTC rule when the user explicitly wants UTC or no wall-clock timezone applies (for example, interval-only cadence). Examples: every 6 hours — FREQ=HOURLY;INTERVAL=6; every day at 9:00 UTC — DTSTART;TZID=UTC:19700101T000000
RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0; weekdays at 13:30 UTC — DTSTART;TZID=UTC:19700101T000000
RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR;BYHOUR=13;BYMINUTE=30; first of the month at 08:00 UTC — DTSTART;TZID=UTC:19700101T000000
RRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=1;BYHOUR=8;BYMINUTE=0. The API rejects malformed rrules; sub-hourly schedules require a Teams plan or above. For a one-time ('run once') schedule, use a DTSTART plus COUNT=1. Preserve a specified timezone with a local wall-clock DTSTART, e.g. 'DTSTART;TZID=America/Los_Angeles:20260115T093000
RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=1'; an explicitly UTC schedule may use 'DTSTART:20260115T173000Z
RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=1'. It fires once then auto-disables. Never fake it with a recurring schedule plus an invocation limit of 1.

actions.description: Actions to run when a trigger fires. Required for create; supported types are start_session, start_code_scan, scan_new_commits, message_session and triage_session. Pass prompt text inline; this runtime does not expand file:// prompt URIs or render BEGIN/END PROMPT blocks.

enabled.description: Enable or disable the automation on 'create'/'update'; on 'list', filter to automations in that enabled state.

notifications.description: Unsupported email/Slack dispatch notifications. The handler rejects notifications; no delivery provider is implied.

tools.description: Unsupported per-automation tool grants. The handler rejects tools; existing runtime allowlists and provider approvals still apply.

metadata.description: Metadata is accepted by this schema but not persisted or queried by the local automation handler; do not rely on it for labels or filters.

limits.description: Resource limits for the automation and the sessions it spawns.

concurrency.description: Caps on simultaneous runs and the queue of events waiting to run.

session_settings.description: Unsupported spawned-session settings. The handler rejects session_settings; mode and network-policy defaults are not inferred.

security_profile.description: Unsupported security-profile binding. The handler rejects security_profile; do not infer network or MCP access.

run_as.description: Unsupported run identity. The handler rejects run_as and does not impersonate an organization or creator.

template_id.description: Create-only provenance marker from the automation templates endpoint.

preflight.description: Unsupported preflight script. Passing preflight to create/update is rejected; preflight_* actions are not implemented and file:// source resolution is unavailable.

queued_event_id.description: Preflight event cursor is unsupported because preflight_* actions are rejected.

run_id.description: Preflight run ID is unsupported because preflight_* actions are rejected.

creator_id.description: Filter 'list' results to automations created by this user id.

event_type.description: Filter 'list' results to automations with a trigger of this event type, e.g. 'slack:message'.

agent_types.description: Filter 'list' results by agent type; multiple values match automations containing at least one action of any given type (OR). Values: 'new_session' (start_session), 'long_running' (message_session), 'triage_session' (auto-triage), 'auto_triage' (legacy monitor_session), 'code_scan' (start_code_scan / scan_new_commits), 'remediate_finding', 'incident_session'.

prompt.description: For 'run' only: free-text stand-in for the triggering event, included in the event payload as additional context (max 10000 chars). Mutually exclusive with event_data.

event_data.description: For 'run' only: structured stand-in for the event data the real source would have sent. Mutually exclusive with prompt.

first.description: Pagination parameter retained for interface compatibility; the local automation list returns stored records without cursor pagination.

after.description: Cursor parameter retained for interface compatibility; the local automation list returns stored records without cursor pagination.

opulent_billing_tag_manage.name: opulent_billing_tag_manage
opulent_billing_tag_manage.description: Manage Opulent billing tags in the runtime store: list/get/create tags, list/add members, and assign a session to a tag one at a time. The hosted bulk assignment and get_session_tags actions are not implemented. This is local tracking, not a hosted billing account or proof of metered charges. Session access remains scoped to this runtime.

billing_tag_id.description: Billing tag id. Required for 'get', 'add_member', 'list_members', and 'assign_session'.

name.description: Billing tag display name. Required for 'create'.

description.description: Free-form description of what work the tag covers. Optional for 'create'.

user_id.description: Member ID to add to a local billing tag. User-management lookup is not provided by this runtime.

opulent_id.description: ID of the Opulent session to assign. Required for 'assign_session'. Assigning replaces the session's current billing tag.

first.description: Pagination hint retained in the schema; local list and list_members return stored rows without paging.

after.description: Opaque cursor for 'list'/'list_members' pagination (from a previous response's end_cursor).

opulent_code_scan_manage.name: opulent_code_scan_manage
opulent_code_scan_manage.description:
Manage repository-scoped Opulent code scans and profiles in this runtime. Establish the scan type first with `list_scan_types`; infer the objective from the request, but only use a type actually returned. Security and other scan types have different profile guidance; never silently broaden a narrow request. Map focus, exclusions and triage guidance from the user’s request; never inline tokens in ingestion guidance — reference configured secret names. Prefer reusing a matching profile over creating an unrelated one.

NEVER call `create_scan` until the user explicitly approves the exact scan and repository in text. A request to set up a scan is not approval to launch it. Repository scope is enforced by the runtime, but no hosted setup form or approval card is implemented here; do not claim that a form submission or card is available. Do not claim a returned scan ID is a hosted scan URL, or that a local scan record proves the investigation completed. The source’s incremental `scan_new_commits`, `update_scan`, and batch `remediate_findings` actions are not implemented by this handler. `remediate_finding` launches code-changing work: use it only on explicit user request, and do not claim PR creation without checking the actual result. Hosted org entitlements, Slack DMs, security-profile approval cards, and MCP grants are not supplied by this adapter.

action.description: Supported local scan actions are list_scans, list_findings, list_scan_types, list_profiles, get_profile, create_profile, update_profile, create_scan, get_session and remediate_finding. list_scan_types returns the local supported types, not organization entitlements. Infer a matching type from the request. Only call create_scan after explicit user approval of the exact repository and objective. get_session returns a local session record, not a hosted link.

time_after.description: Unix seconds lower bound. Optional creation-time filter ('list_scans' only).

time_before.description: Unix seconds upper bound. Optional creation-time filter ('list_scans' only).

repo_name.description: Filter to this repository ('list_scans' and 'list_findings'), or the full repository name to scan ('create_scan'; provide exactly one of repo_name or repos).

host.description: Git host of the repository/repositories ('create_scan' only).

repos.description: Full names of the repositories to scan together as one scan ('create_scan'; provide exactly one of repo_name or repos). The first entry is the scan's primary repo. Use this whenever the user wants more than one repository covered.

interactive.description: Accepted in the schema but ignored by the local create_scan handler. It does not pause investigation or open a hosted user review session.

effort.description: Accepted in the schema but ignored by the local create_scan handler. It does not select a model, ACU budget, investigation pipeline or validation depth.

scan_id.description: Filter findings to this scan ('list_findings'), or the scan ID containing the finding ('remediate_finding'), or the scan whose orchestrating session to retrieve ('get_session').

profile_id.description: The profile ID. Required for 'get_profile' and 'update_profile'; optional for 'create_scan'.

scan_type.description: Type of scan, e.g. 'security' or 'general' ('create_scan', 'create_profile', 'list_profiles'). For 'list_profiles': only return profiles for this scan type — always pass the chosen type so profiles for other types are never shown or considered. For 'create_scan': must match the chosen profile's scan type; defaults to the profile's type, or 'security' when neither a profile nor a type is given. Every non-security scan type requires a profile_id — the profile defines the scan's objective. For 'create_profile': the type of scan the profile configures (defaults to 'security'). For 'update_profile': the new scan type of the profile.

profile_name.description: Name of the profile. Required for 'create_profile'; optional new name for 'update_profile'.

mode.description: Profile mode: 'discover' (default) or 'ingest' ('create_profile' only; the mode is fixed at creation).

include_globs.description: Glob patterns of files to include in scans ('create_profile' and 'update_profile').

exclude_globs.description: Glob patterns of files to exclude from scans ('create_profile' and 'update_profile').

threat_model_guidance.description: Guidance describing the threat model ('create_profile' and 'update_profile').

investigation_guidance.description: Guidance for the investigation phase ('create_profile' and 'update_profile').

triage_guidance.description: Guidance for the triage phase ('create_profile' and 'update_profile').

validation_guidance.description: Guidance for the validation phase ('create_profile' and 'update_profile').

report_guidance.description: Guidance for the report phase ('create_profile' and 'update_profile').

communication_guidance.description: Optional text stored on a local scan profile. The local scan worker does not send Slack DMs or run a separate communication phase; do not promise notifications.

remediation_guidance.description: Guidance for the remediation phase ('create_profile' and 'update_profile').

ingestion_source_guidance.description: Guidance describing the ingestion source ('create_profile' and 'update_profile').

post_ingestion_guidance.description: Guidance for the post-ingestion phase ('create_profile' and 'update_profile').

severity.description: Filter findings to these severities: 'critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low' ('list_findings' only).

status.description: Filter findings to these statuses: 'open', 'dismissed', 'resolved' ('list_findings' only).

first.description: Page size for list actions (default 100, max 200).

after.description: Opaque cursor for list pagination (from a previous response's end_cursor).

action.description: Operation to perform. Notes: 'list', 'get', 'create', 'update', 'delete', 'folders' (returns the folder structure with per-folder note counts). Suggestions: 'list_suggestions', 'view_suggestion', 'dismiss_suggestions'.

note_id.description: Note ID — required for get, update, delete.

name.description: Note name — required for create and update (v3 PUT is full-replace).

content.description: Note content — required for create and update (v3 PUT is full-replace).

trigger.description: Trigger description — required for create and update (v3 PUT is full-replace).

pinned_repo.description: Pin this note to a specific repo (owner/repo format). For create/update: sets the pinned repo. For list: filters results to notes pinned to this repo.

search.description: Search query for 'list' — case-insensitive substring match across note name, trigger, and content. Useful for dedup and conflict detection.

folder_path.description: Filter 'list' results to notes in a specific folder (e.g. 'Dana/SubFolder' or '/' for root notes only).

after.description: Opaque cursor for 'list' pagination (from a previous response's end_cursor).

event_id.description: Event ID of a knowledge suggestion — required for view_suggestion.

event_ids.description: List of event IDs to dismiss — required for dismiss_suggestions.

query.description: Search query for list_suggestions — filters by trigger/content text.

since_days.description: Only return suggestions from the last N days (list_suggestions).

body.description: Deprecated alias for `content`. Prefer `content`; this is accepted only for backward compatibility with older callers/skills.

opulent_mcp.name: opulent_mcp
opulent_mcp.description: Runtime-local connector facade. 'list_tools' lists registered local handler names, not their parameter schemas or an external MCP server's tools; listed names may still be forbidden by the active execution policy. 'call_tool' dispatches one runtime-local handler by tool_name and obeys its normal allowlist, authentication and approval checks. Discover external or native MCP tools (including native lx_* tools) with mcp_list_tools and server; invoke them with mcp_call_tool with server, name and arguments. opulent_mcp does not invoke them.

command.description: The Opulent MCP operation to perform.

tool_name.description: Name of the tool to execute (required for call_tool command).

tool_args.description: JSON string containing an object of runtime-local tool arguments (optional for call_tool). File URLs are not expanded automatically.

opulent_mcp_server_manage.name: opulent_mcp_server_manage
opulent_mcp_server_manage.description: Manage MCP server installation requests and enable/disable records. For a custom installation, research the official endpoint and authentication method; never ask the user to paste a secret into ordinary session text. Reference only an approved environment-variable secret name and an allowlisted HTTPS URL or stdio command. `install`, `update`, and `delete` create pending approval requests; they do not install a server immediately. Only a separate approval flow can probe and activate a server. Do not claim an automatic approval card or private-mode hosting. Verify a provider connection with `mcp_list_tools` before treating an enabled record as working.

action.description: Operation to perform. 'resolve_install' is read-only: it resolves marketplace_server_slug and returns the server identity, default credential scope, URL, and any selectable url_options (e.g. regions).

installation_id.description: Installation id. Required for 'update', 'delete', 'enable', and 'disable'. Find it with list_integrations.

marketplace_server_slug.description: For 'install': the marketplace server's slug or exact name (e.g. 'notion' or 'Notion'); no prior list_integrations call is needed. Transport, command, and auth come from the marketplace manifest and cannot be overridden; url may only select a variant the manifest allows. Omit to install a custom server.

name.description: Display name. Required for a custom 'install'.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier for the installation. Required for a custom 'install'.

short_description.description: One-line description. Required for a custom 'install'.

url.description: Server URL. Required for HTTP/SSE transport on a custom 'install'. On a marketplace 'install', only to select a URL variant (e.g. a region): it must keep the scheme and host of one of the manifest's URLs; omit it for the default.

command.description: Command to run. Required for STDIO transport on a custom 'install'.

auth_method.description: 'none', 'auth_header', or 'oauth'. Credential values themselves cannot be set through this tool — a person supplies them on the settings configure page.

installation_scope.description: Optional override: 'org' (Organization) shares one credential org-wide; 'user' (Personal) has each member connect their own account. Omit unless the user requests a scope; the marketplace default (or 'org') applies.

oauth_resource.description: OAuth resource indicator. Custom installs only.

icon.description: Optional icon value retained in the schema; the local handler does not create an approval card or automatically set this field.

opulent_oncall_manage.name: opulent_oncall_manage
opulent_oncall_manage.description: Manage Opulent on-call responder, incident, and report records in this runtime. Call `schemas` for locally supported resources and triggers before creating a responder; responders require one Slack-message trigger constrained to a real channel ID. Never invent Slack channel IDs. Use `validate_create`/`validate_update` to dry-run and list before retrying an ambiguous create. Obtain explicit user approval before creating, updating, deleting, stopping, resuming, or ingesting a dashboard. Hosted PagerDuty, incident settings, approval cards, automatic Slack delivery, identity/network policy, and organization-specific merge semantics are not supplied here. Check actual connected providers and returned run status before claiming incident triage succeeded.

AutomationConditionGroupSpec.description: AND-group: every condition in the group must match.

AutomationConditionSpec.description: A single field/operator/value filter on the triggering event.

field.description: Event field used by local conditions. On-call responders require a Slack channel ID condition; do not use a channel name or #handle.

operator.description: Comparison operator; the operators each field supports come from action="schemas".

value.description: Comparison value; its type follows the operator (string/number/bool for eq/neq, string for contains/matches, [low, high] numbers for between, string list for in/not_in/globs, RRULE string for recurrence, omitted for is_empty/is_not_empty).

AutomationConditionsSpec.description: Event filter: OR of AND-groups (fixed two-level DNF).

AutomationInvocationLimitsSpec.description: Rate limit on the automation's own firing.

max_per_window.description: Maximum trigger firings per rolling window.

window_seconds.description: Length of the rolling window in seconds.

AutomationIpv4DestinationSpec.description: Allowed IPv4 address or CIDR block.

AutomationIpv6DestinationSpec.description: Allowed IPv6 address or CIDR block.

max_acu_limit.description: ACU limit retained in the schema but not metered or enforced by the local on-call handler.

invocations.description: Rate-limits the automation's own firing. Omitted/null = unlimited.

AutomationNetPolicySpec.description: Network policy restricting spawned sessions' outbound connections.

allow.description: Destinations spawned sessions may reach; everything else is blocked.

AutomationReplySpec.description: Where the trigger's spawned session binds and its response is delivered.

type.description: notify_thread: one-way 'session started' breadcrumb in the triggering Slack thread; attach_thread: two-way binding to the triggering Slack thread (both Slack triggers only, and they can't be combined); post_response: deliver the agent's response to the triggering context.

AutomationRunAsSpec.description: Identity that triggered sessions run as and are attributed to.

type.description: Unsupported on-call run identity. The handler rejects run_as and does not impersonate a creator or organization user.

AutomationSlackChannelSpec.description: Slack channel the spawned sessions' Slack tools may post to.

OncallReportNotificationsSpec.description: Where report runs are delivered (create-time only in this version).

channel_id.description: Slack channel ID (e.g. C0123ABC456) each report run is delivered to.

OncallSessionConfigSpec.description: Session-level config for spawned sessions (same shape as automations' actions[].session).

tags.description: Unsupported on-call session tags. The handler rejects the session group and does not validate hosted cost codes.

OncallSessionSettingsSpec.description: Settings applied to the sessions a responder / incident spawns.

opulent_mode.description: Unsupported on-call session setting. The handler rejects session_settings; no organization mode default is selected.

net_policy.description: Unsupported on-call network setting. The handler rejects session_settings; null does not grant unrestricted access.

OncallToolsSpec.description: Tool grants for spawned sessions (subset of automations' tools group).

mcp_servers.description: Authoritative allowlist of MCP server marketplace slugs (e.g. 'datadog', 'sentry') the sessions may use; omitted/empty = no MCP tools. Only recommend telemetry servers the organization has actually installed (check list_integrations first).

slack_channels.description: Slack channels the sessions' Slack tools may post to (a tool grant, not trigger matching). Incident sessions may also be granted all public channels via incident settings.

linear_enabled.description: Unsupported per-responder Linear grant. The handler rejects tools; any Linear provider requires separate configuration.

OncallTriggerSpec.description: A responder trigger — the automations trigger shape restricted to slack:message.

event_type.description: Only 'slack:message' is accepted; a responder triages one Slack channel.

conditions.description: Automation-style DNF filter {'any': [{'all': [...]}]}. Every AND group must include a positive 'channel' condition (operator eq/in) naming the Slack channel ID (e.g. C0123ABC456, never the #name); extra filters (user, text) are allowed.

replies.description: Must be empty: responders manage their own thread replies.

action.description: Local actions depend on resource: responder list/get/create/validate_create/update/validate_update/delete/issues/run/stop/resume; incident list/get/stop/resume; report list/get/create/validate_create/update/validate_update/delete/runs/run. Without a resource, schemas and ingest_dashboard are supported. Other legacy enum values are not uniformly implemented; verify the returned result.

resource.description: Use responder, incident, or report. incident_settings remains in the enum for interface compatibility but is rejected by this runtime.

report_id.description: Report id for report get/update/validate_update/delete/runs/run, and the optional filter for incident list (returns that report's candidate period + incidents to classify).

after.description: Opaque cursor for list/issues/runs pagination (from a previous response).

order_by.description: Issue ordering for responder 'issues': 'last_activity' (default) or 'occurrence_count'. A cursor is only valid for the ordering it was minted under.

name.description: Display name for responder/report create (required) or update.

enabled.description: Responder: whether it triages new messages (default true). incident_settings: whether the incident feature is on for the org.

triggers.description: Responder create (required)/update: exactly one 'slack:message' trigger whose conditions name the Slack channel ID to triage, e.g. [{'event_type': 'slack:message', 'conditions': {'any': [{'all': [{'field': 'channel', 'operator': 'eq', 'value': 'C0123ABC456'}]}]}}]. Ask the user for the channel ID (or find it via list_integrations / Slack tools); never invent one. On update the list replaces wholesale.

team_id.description: Slack workspace (team) ID for the responder's channel; omit when the org has one workspace.

runbook.description: Responder investigation instructions. Omit by default — the server applies 'Investigate the root cause to the best of your abilities.' Only supply one when the user gives concrete investigation steps; pass '' on update to reset to the default.

tools.description: Unsupported responder tool grants. The handler rejects tools; check provider configuration separately.

metadata.description: Responder labels. Recommend {'team': ...} always and {'service': ...} when obvious from the channel/runbook; reports can select members by these tags (responder_tags). Update merges per key; a null value deletes the key.

limits.description: Invocation limits may be recorded for a responder, but max_acu_limit requires a metering backend and is not enforced here. Do not assume a hosted default rate.

session_settings.description: Unsupported responder session mode/network policy. The handler rejects session_settings; no hosted organization defaults or unrestricted-null behavior.

session.description: Unsupported on-call session tags and cost codes. The handler rejects the session group.

run_as.description: Unsupported on-call identity switch. The handler rejects run_as; it does not promise a hosted organization system user.

slack_channel_prefix.description: Incident-settings channel prefix is unsupported because this runtime excludes incident_settings.

auto_join_enabled.description: Incident-settings auto-join is unsupported because this runtime excludes incident_settings.

slack_team_id.description: incident_settings: Slack workspace ID incidents are watched in (omit for one workspace). Pass '' on update to clear the stored workspace.

responder_automation_ids.description: Report create/update: fixed responder membership (ids from responder list). Mutually exclusive with responder_tags; on update the list replaces wholesale.

responder_tags.description: Report create/update: tag-managed membership — every responder whose metadata matches ALL these key/values (e.g. {'team': 'payments'}), resolved live at each run. Preferred when the user describes members by team/service.

incidents_match.description: Report create/update: natural-language description of which incidents belong in this report (e.g. 'incidents affecting the payments service'). Omit for a responders-only report; pass '' on update to clear it.

notifications.description: Unsupported report Slack delivery. The report handler rejects notifications; a generated report is not automatically posted.

incident_ids.description: Report 'runs' POST: incident ids classified into the report for this period (from incident list with report_id). Supplying this (even []) submits a run instead of listing runs.

summary.description: Report 'runs' POST: at-most-2-sentence overview of the period vs the previous run.

report.description: Report 'runs' POST: the full report body in markdown.

dashboard.description: 'ingest_dashboard': reference to the dashboard to ingest — a URL, id, or name.

opulent_playbook_manage.name: opulent_playbook_manage
opulent_playbook_manage.description: Manage Opulent playbooks with a single action-based tool in the runtime store; it does not synchronize hosted playbooks.

title.description: Playbook title. Required for 'create' and 'update' (v3 PUT is full-replace).

content.description: Playbook markdown content. Required for 'create' and 'update' (v3 PUT is full-replace).

macro.description: Automation macro identifier. Must start with '!' followed by word characters (letters, digits, underscores), e.g. '!my_macro'. Optional.

structured_output_schema.description: JSON Schema (Draft 7) defining the required output contract for sessions using this playbook. Max 64KB. Optional for 'create' and 'update'.

after.description: Opaque cursor for 'list' pagination (from a previous response's end_cursor).

body.description: Deprecated alias for `content`. Prefer `content`; this is accepted only for backward compatibility with older callers/skills.

opulent_review_manage.name: opulent_review_manage
opulent_review_manage.description: Trigger an Opulent review for an allowlisted repository’s pull request, get its status, or fetch its findings when the configured review worker supports those actions. Reviews may run asynchronously: fetch status before requesting findings. This runtime does not establish a hosted private-mode organization or grant repository access; verify credentials and the returned review result before claiming completion.

action.description: 'trigger' starts a Opulent Review for the PR; 'get_status' fetches the latest review status for the PR; 'get_findings' fetches the findings of a completed review. By default, only the severities the org delivers to sessions are returned; the rest remain available on the Opulent Review page and can be fetched by passing the severity explicitly.

pr_url.description: Full URL of the pull/merge request (e.g. 'https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123').

commit_sha.description: get_status/get_findings only: commit SHA to look up (full or short prefix). Defaults to the PR's current head commit.

severity.description: get_findings only: filter findings to one severity ('bug', 'security', 'flag', or 'info'). Bug means a concrete correctness, regression, or repo-rule violation; security means a vulnerability or hardening gap; flag means something needing further investigation that may or may not be a bug; info means an informational note. Omit to return only the severities the org delivers to sessions; the remaining severities stay available on the Opulent Review page and can be fetched by passing the severity explicitly.

opulent_schedule_manage.name: opulent_schedule_manage
opulent_schedule_manage.description: Manage existing scheduled Opulent sessions in this runtime. Legacy `create` is unavailable: use `opulent_automation_manage` with a `schedule:recurring` trigger. Existing schedule actions still use their recorded local configuration. Do not claim a hosted migration state or a provider’s 403 response.

action.description: Manage existing local schedules with list, get, update or delete. Legacy create remains in the enum for compatibility but the handler rejects it; create a recurring automation instead.

schedule_id.description: The schedule ID. Required for 'get', 'update', and 'delete'.

name.description: Human-readable name for the schedule. Required for 'create'.

prompt.description: The prompt Opulent will run on each trigger. Required for 'create'.

playbook_id.description: Optional playbook to attach to the scheduled session.

frequency.description: Cron expression (e.g. '0 9 * * 1-5'). Required for 'create' with recurring schedules.

scheduled_at.description: ISO 8601 datetime to run at. Required for 'create' with one_time schedules.

enabled.description: Enable or disable the schedule (used with 'update').

bypass_approval.description: Unsupported approval bypass. This field does not disable tool permission checks in this runtime.

target_opulent_id.description: Opulent session ID to send the prompt to instead of starting a new session. Only valid for one_time schedules. Use this to schedule a message to be sent to an existing session at a future time (e.g. to wake yourself up later).

platform.description: Platform value retained in the schema but not used by the local schedule handler to select a VM or validate an organization platform.

limit.description: Max number of results for 'list' (capped at 100).

opulent_session_create.name: opulent_session_create
opulent_session_create.description: Create one or more child Opulent sessions in this runtime. Only use this when prompted to; do not parallelize by default. Children must use repositories in the configured allowlist. Returned IDs identify locally owned child sessions; pass them unchanged to `opulent_session_interact`. This is not the hosted v3 REST API and does not expose organization-wide sessions.

SessionSpec.description:
A single session to create. Only 'prompt' is required; the per-session
fields override the batch-level arguments for that session. Agent mode
(`opulent_mode`) is batch-level only and cannot be set per session.

title.description: Title for the session (auto-generated when omitted).

playbook_id.description: ID of a playbook to run the session with.

tags.description: Per-session override of the batch-level tags arg.

notify_only_on_user_message.description: Only notify users who have sent a message in this session.

repos.description: Per-session override of the batch-level repos arg.

platform.description: Per-session platform value retained in the schema; local startSession ignores VM/outpost placement overrides.

attachment_urls.description: Already-uploaded attachment URLs to attach to the initial prompt.

board_ticket_ids.description: Opulent Boards ticket ids this session is started to work on (from opulent_ticket_manage). Per-session override of the batch-level board_ticket_ids arg. The child session claims the tickets itself; the caller must not claim them.

notify_on_response.description: When true, you are notified (and woken if sleeping) once when this child next settles (finishes, blocks, or exits). One-shot: consumed on delivery — pass notify_on_response again on a later message to re-subscribe.

structured_output_schema.description: Per-session override of the batch-level structured_output_schema arg.

structured_output_required.description: Flag retained in the schema but not enforced by local startSession. A supplied structured_output_schema is validated against the child final response.

triage_issue_id.description: Auto-triage: ID of the issue this investigation session works on.

triage_invocation_id.description: Auto-triage: ID of the issue occurrence that spawned this investigation session.

incident_slack_channel.description: Incident response: ID of the incident Slack channel containing the thread to bind this child to.

incident_slack_thread_ts.description: Incident response: any message ts in the incident Slack thread to bind this child to.

sessions.description: Array of session specs; only 'prompt' is required in each.

structured_output_schema.description: JSON Schema applied to created children without a per-session override. A child is asked to return JSON matching the schema, and final output is validated locally; no provide_structured_output tool or hosted polling contract is involved.

repos.description: List of repository identifiers in 'owner/repo' format (e.g. ['myorg/myrepo']) to restrict ALL created sessions to. Each session spec can also include a 'repos' key to override this value for that session.

platform.description: Batch platform value retained in the schema; local startSession ignores VM/outpost placement overrides.

tags.description: Tags to apply to ALL created sessions (e.g. a shared run or campaign identifier). Each session spec can also include a 'tags' key to override this value for that session.

board_ticket_ids.description: Ticket IDs retained in the schema but not validated, claimed or dispatched by local startSession.

opulent_mode.description: Agent mode value retained in the schema but not used by local startSession to select a hosted mode or enterprise feature flag.

opulent_session_events.name: opulent_session_events
opulent_session_events.description: Inspect events within a child Opulent session owned by this runtime. Actions: `list` returns paginated summaries; `details` returns full selected events or an offset range; `search` filters locally recorded event contents. This is not an organization-wide hosted event search.

session_id.description: Target Opulent session ID (must include 'opulent-' prefix).

event_types.description: Filter by event type strings (list/search only, mutually exclusive with categories).

categories.description: Filter by category — shell, file, search, browser, mcp, git, message, status, secret, todo, recording, knowledge, playbook, webhook, lifecycle, other (list/search only, mutually exclusive with event_types).

event_ids.description: Event IDs to fetch full contents for (details only, max 20, mutually exclusive with offset).

offset.description: 0-based offset into the session timeline for details (details only, mutually exclusive with event_ids). Use with limit.

limit.description: Number of events to fetch when using offset (details only, default 20, max 50).

max_content_length.description: Max chars per large content field in details (default 10000).

query.description: Search text (search only, required for search action).

opulent_session_interact.name: opulent_session_interact
opulent_session_interact.description: Interact with a child Opulent session owned by this runtime. `get` returns the local session record and child IDs; `message` sends to an active or sleeping child; `sleep`/`terminate` cancel the child; `archive`/`unarchive` update local archive state. `get_messages` returns locally recorded messages with pagination, `get_attachments` returns recorded pointers, and `set_tags` replaces tags. A completed child cannot be resumed by `message`. Do not claim hosted webapp URLs, ACU usage, PR metadata, or automatic notifications unless the returned record actually provides them.

action.description: Operation to perform — get, message, sleep, terminate, archive, unarchive, get_messages, get_attachments, set_tags.

session_id.description: Target Opulent session ID, e.g. 'opulent-abc123...' (the 'opulent-' prefix is optional — bare IDs, such as the ones in child_session_ids, also work).

attachment_urls.description: Optional list of already-uploaded attachment URLs to attach to the message (only used when action is 'message'). Each URL must belong to the session's org — same mechanism as the initial prompt's attachments.

tags.description: Tag list (required when action is 'set_tags'). Replaces all existing tags on the session — this is a full replacement, not a union/append.

notify_on_response.description: Only used when action is 'message'. When true, you are notified (and woken if sleeping) once when this session next settles (finishes, blocks, or exits). One-shot: consumed on delivery — pass it again on a later message to re-subscribe. Works for any session you are allowed to message (children and same-automation siblings).

archive_on_terminate.description: Also archive the session when terminating (default False).

first.description: Page size for get_messages pagination (v3 cursor param). get_attachments is not paginated — v3 returns the full list.

after.description: Opaque cursor for get_messages pagination (v3 cursor param).

opulent_session_search.name: opulent_session_search
opulent_session_search.description: Search and filter child Opulent sessions owned by this runtime. All supplied filters combine with AND. Returned `session_id` values are local IDs; use them unchanged with `opulent_session_interact`. This is not an organization-wide hosted search.

session_ids.description: Filter to specific session IDs (must include the 'opulent-' prefix, e.g. 'opulent-abc123...').

created_after.description: Unix timestamp lower bound for creation time.

created_before.description: Unix timestamp upper bound for creation time.

updated_after.description: Unix timestamp lower bound for update time.

updated_before.description: Unix timestamp upper bound for update time.

parent_session_id.description: Filter to child sessions spawned by this parent session (accepts the 'opulent-' prefix).

first.description: Number of results per page (default 20, max 100 — tool-level cap below server's 200).

after.description: Opaque cursor for pagination (from a previous response's end_cursor).

download_attachment.name: download_attachment
download_attachment.description: Download a `storage://` attachment pointer in the configured artifact repository, or a public HTTP(S) URL, to the sandbox workspace and return its path. Use this when you need an attachment’s bytes locally. Passing multiple `urls` downloads them in one call. This does not authenticate to arbitrary hosted session attachment URLs; a provider-specific credential is required for those.

url.description: The Opulent attachment URL to download. The file will be downloaded to the box and its local path returned.

urls.description: A list of Opulent attachment URLs to download. Use this instead of url when downloading multiple attachments at once.

edit.name: edit
edit.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files.

Usage:
- Read the file before editing so old_string matches the current text.
- Preserve exact indentation from the file content when matching old_string; do not include display line numbers.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files to creating new ones.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- The edit will fail if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
- Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

old_string.description: The text to replace. Always provide old_string before new_string so that streaming displays can show the diff progressively.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false).

exec.name: exec
exec.description:
Execute a shell command in the sandbox and return its output, or a shell_id for a still-running process. Commands use the sandbox command environment; one-shot calls do not preserve a working directory. Set `workdir` to an existing absolute directory when needed, and use a returned `shell_id` to continue an interactive process.

Use specialized file tools for reading, writing, editing, and searching files when possible. Check the intended parent directory before a command that creates files; quote paths containing spaces and never embed secrets in commands. Chain dependent commands with `&&` so later steps run only if earlier ones succeed. Do not assume a Windows shell, automatic sudo authorization, or a persistent shell on calls without shell_id.

command.description: The command to execute in the current shell session.

shell_id.description: Optional shell ID to reuse an existing interactive session. Use shell IDs to maintain multiple shell sessions. When shell ID is provided, writes to that session's stdin. When no shell ID is provided, a new session is created.

workdir.description: Optional absolute path to use as the working directory for this command (does not persist between one-shot calls; with a shell_id it cds the session).

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (default: background after 10s idle or 30s total). When it elapses, a still-running command is backgrounded and its shell_id returned for get_output/kill_shell. Set to 0 to background immediately.

tty.description: Allocate a PTY-backed interactive session. Default false. false (default): one-shot non-interactive command run through pipes; good for most use cases. true: persistent interactive session — for TUI programs (vim, tmux, top, REPLs) or state that must persist across calls.

fetch_pr_template.name: fetch_pr_template
fetch_pr_template.description: Fetch the PR template for a repository. You must call this before creating or updating a PR so you can write a PR body that follows the repo's template. Returns the template (falling back to a default if the repo has none).

include_diff.description: If true, also return the cumulative merge-base diff against base_branch. Defaults to false.

base_branch.description: The branch you intend to merge into (e.g., 'main', 'master'). Only used when include_diff is true.

exec_dir.description: Optional path to the repository on the box (e.g., '/home/user/repos/myrepo'). Overrides the auto-derived path from the repo registry.

find_file_by_name.name: find_file_by_name
find_file_by_name.description: Fast file name/path pattern matching in the workspace. Matches names or relative paths, not file contents. Do NOT use this tool for searching function names or variables; use `grep` for contents. Patterns follow the runtime’s fnmatch implementation, not ripgrep glob brace expansion.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against.

path.description: The directory to search in (defaults to current working directory)

generate_image.name: generate_image
generate_image.description: Generate an image from a text prompt. The image is returned as base64; an optional `output_path` saves it inside the sandbox workspace. Useful for logos, illustrations, placeholder assets, mockups, and other visual content. Pass input_image_paths to edit or combine existing images on the machine (e.g. restyle a screenshot or apply a logo to a mockup) instead of generating from scratch. Use `upload_attachment` to create an artifact pointer if storage is configured, or pass the saved workspace path to `message_user` attachments. The image provider requires configured credentials; do not claim an image was produced before the call succeeds.

prompt.description: Text prompt describing the image to generate. Be extremely specific and write a self-contained description.

output_path.description: Path on the machine where the generated image is saved. The file extension controls the format (.png, .jpg/.jpeg, or .webp; PNG by default).

input_image_paths.description: Paths to existing image files on the machine to use as input/reference images.

size.description: Image dimensions as '{width}x{height}'. Defaults to the model choosing automatically.

quality.description: Rendering quality: 'low', 'medium', or 'high'. Defaults to the model choosing automatically.

get_knowledge_note.name: get_knowledge_note
get_knowledge_note.description: Retrieve the full body of a knowledge note. For smaller notes (under ~12000 characters), the content is returned directly in this tool's output. For larger notes, the body is written to knowledge/<note_id>.md under the home directory.

knowledge_id.description: ID of the knowledge note to download (from the <knowledge id=...> attribute, e.g. 'note-abc123'). Use list_knowledge_notes to discover available IDs.

get_output.name: get_output
get_output.description: Reads output from a background shell process using the `shell_id` returned by `exec`. A timeout is a maximum wait and returns when the process exits; the process continues running after output is read. Use a longer timeout to await a finite command and a shorter one to inspect startup output from a server. Output may be incremental; inspect the returned running and exit status rather than treating an empty chunk as completion.

shell_id.description: The ID of the shell to read output from.

incremental.description: If true (default), returns only output produced since the last read. If false, returns the full output buffer. If a previously returned line has changed since the last read (e.g. an in-place progress bar), it is returned again in full.

get_workflow_output.name: get_workflow_output
get_workflow_output.description: Wait for or check on a workflow run that is executing in the background (a `run_workflow` call that was interrupted keeps its run alive). Returns the run's final output once it finishes, or a progress snapshot if it is still running when the wait elapses: its agents' statuses plus the script's recent output, including its log() lines emitted so far.

run_id.description: The backgrounded run to wait on: the run_id ("wfr-...") reported by run_workflow.

timeout_secs.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the run to finish (default 60, max 7 days). If it is still running when the wait elapses, a progress snapshot of its agents and recent log() output is returned instead.

git_add_labels.name: git_add_labels
git_add_labels.description: Add labels to a pull request.

git_ci_job_logs.name: git_ci_job_logs
git_ci_job_logs.description: Fetch logs for a specific CI job. Use the job_id from git_pr_checks output.

git_close_pr.name: git_close_pr
git_close_pr.description: Close a pull request without merging.

git_comment_on_pr.name: git_comment_on_pr
git_comment_on_pr.description: Post a comment on a pull request. Supports general comments, inline code comments on specific lines, and replies to existing comments.

body.description: Comment body in markdown format. Pass the body inline, or as a single file:// URI.

path.description: File path for inline code comments (optional, requires line parameter).

line.description: Line number for inline code comments (optional, requires path parameter).

side.description: Side of diff for inline comments: LEFT for old code, RIGHT for new code (optional, defaults to RIGHT).

commit_id.description: Commit SHA for inline PR comments. Optional; auto-resolved from the PR head if omitted.

in_reply_to.description: Comment ID to reply to (optional). Only works for file (review) comments, not top-level comments.

git_create_pr.name: git_create_pr
git_create_pr.description: Create a new pull request. Make sure your branch is pushed to the remote before calling this tool. You must call fetch_pr_template for this repo first.

draft.description: Whether to create a Draft PR or Open PR.

base_branch.description: The branch you want to merge into (e.g., 'main', 'master').

body.description: Pull request description/body. Pass the body inline, or as a single file:// URI to have it replaced with that file's contents on the box.

git_delete_comment.name: git_delete_comment
git_delete_comment.description: Delete a general comment you previously posted on a pull request. Use this to clean up duplicate, outdated, or accidental comments so the PR conversation stays tidy.

comment_id.description: ID of the comment to delete (as returned when the comment was posted).

git_edit_comment.name: git_edit_comment
git_edit_comment.description: Edit a general comment you posted earlier in this session on a pull request, replacing its body. Prefer editing an existing comment over posting a new one when updating status. Only works for general (top-level) PR comments, not inline review comments.

comment_id.description: ID of the comment to edit (as returned when the comment was posted).

body.description: New comment body in markdown format. Pass the body inline, or as a single file:// URI.

git_list_repos.name: git_list_repos
git_list_repos.description: List the Git repositories (GitHub, GitLab, etc.) that you have access to. Returns repository names, URLs, descriptions, and languages. Use the filter_name parameter to search for specific repositories by name.

filter_name.description: Filter repositories by name (case-insensitive substring match). Optional.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based, default: 1). Each page shows up to 30 repositories.

git_pr_checks.name: git_pr_checks
git_pr_checks.description: Check the CI status of a pull request. Shows pass/fail/pending status for each check. Supports multiple wait modes: all (default), failure, stage, none.

wait_mode.description: Wait mode: 'all' to wait for all checks, 'failure' to wait until any check fails, 'stage' to wait for a specific stage, 'none' for an immediate snapshot.

stage.description: Stage name to wait for (required when wait_mode is 'stage').

git_remove_labels.name: git_remove_labels
git_remove_labels.description: Remove labels from a pull request.

git_take_over_pr.name: git_take_over_pr
git_take_over_pr.description: Take over an existing pull request that wasn't created in this session. This attaches the PR to your current session so you receive live notifications for the rest of the session.

git_update_pr.name: git_update_pr
git_update_pr.description: Update an existing pull request's title and/or body. You must call fetch_pr_template for this repo first.

body.description: New body/description (optional). Pass the body inline, or as a single file:// URI.

force.description: If true, force update the PR even if its description or title has been modified independently.

git_update_pr_base.name: git_update_pr_base
git_update_pr_base.description: Change the base (target) branch of a pull request.

git_view_pr.name: git_view_pr
git_view_pr.description: View details of a pull request including title, description, comments, CI status summary, and merge conflict status. For viewing the full diff, use git diff --merge-base origin/<base_branch> in the shell.

grep.name: grep
grep.description: Search workspace file contents with a regular expression. Filter files with `glob_pattern`; choose `content`, `files_with_matches`, or `count` through `output_mode`, and use `case_insensitive` and `context_lines` as needed. This runtime uses Python regular expressions, not ripgrep/Rust regex, and walks only workspace paths. If results are truncated, narrow your search with a more specific pattern or filters.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for, passed to ripgrep under the hood

path.description: The directory or file to search in. Required — prefer an absolute path.

glob_pattern.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g., '*.rs' searches .rs files in current dir but not subdirs, 'src/**/*.py' searches .py files in src/ and its subdirs). Defaults to searching all files.

case_insensitive.description: Perform case-insensitive search. Defaults to false.

max_results.description: Maximum number of matches to return. Defaults to 100, max 20,000. Only applicable for content output mode.

context_lines.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (context). Defaults to 0.

kill_shell.name: kill_shell
kill_shell.description:
Kills a running background shell by its ID.

- Takes a shell_id parameter identifying the shell to kill
- Returns the shell_id, whether it was killed, and its exit code
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running shell

shell_id.description: The ID of the shell to kill.

kill_workflow.name: kill_workflow
kill_workflow.description: Kill a running workflow by run_id. The script is cancelled; completed child results remain recorded and unfinished children are cancelled. The recorded run can be inspected afterward, but do not assume it can be resumed unless `run_workflow` succeeds with its run_id.

run_id.description: The run to kill: the run_id ("wfr-...") reported by run_workflow.

linear.name: linear
linear.description: Tool for interacting with Linear via MCP. Available commands: 'list_tools' (lists all available Linear tools like list_issues, get_issue, save_issue, etc.), 'call_tool' (executes a specific Linear tool with the provided JSON arguments). Use list_tools first to see what operations are available. Requires a configured, approved and reachable Linear MCP server; listing a handler alone does not prove connectivity.

command.description: The Linear MCP operation to perform.

tool_name.description: Name of the tool to execute (required for call_tool command).

tool_args.description: JSON string containing the input arguments for the tool (optional for call_tool command).

list_integrations.name: list_integrations
list_integrations.description: List native integrations and MCP servers recorded for this runtime, with their stored status. Returns `integrations` and `mcp_servers`; pass `query` to narrow the names. Stored or marketplace entries are not evidence of a working provider connection. Check the specific provider and authorization before making a live claim; do not fabricate hosted settings URLs.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against name, slug, and description. Use it whenever you are looking for one specific integration or MCP server (e.g. query='whimsical'); the unfiltered catalog is large.

list_knowledge_notes.name: list_knowledge_notes
list_knowledge_notes.description: List all knowledge notes available in this session. Each entry shows the note's id, name, scope (when this note is normally retrieved), author (user or system), and the size of the note body in characters. Notes with bodies larger than ~3000 characters are middle-truncated when injected into the conversation.

list_secrets.name: list_secrets
list_secrets.description: List available secrets configured for this session. Shows secret names and types, but not values. Use ${SECRET_NAME} syntax in shell commands to reference a secret value.

filter.description: Optional: filter to show only org or session secrets. Values: 'org', 'session', or 'all' (default).

mcp_call_tool.name: mcp_call_tool
mcp_call_tool.description: Execute a tool on an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server with the provided JSON arguments. Requires a configured, approved server and allowlisted transport; verify the provider is connected and authorized rather than inferring that from the handler.

mcp_list_servers.name: mcp_list_servers
mcp_list_servers.description: List MCP server records configured in this runtime. Use this to check names and stored enable/approval state. A record alone does not establish a live connection; use `mcp_list_tools` to verify the provider is reachable and authorized.

mcp_list_tools.name: mcp_list_tools
mcp_list_tools.description: List the tools and resources available on a specific MCP (Model Context Protocol) server. This connects through the approved and allowlisted server transport; a failure must remain visible, not be treated as an empty list.

mcp_read_resource.name: mcp_read_resource
mcp_read_resource.description: Read a resource from an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server by URI. MCP servers can expose resources (data addressable by URI) in addition to tools; use this to dereference resource URIs returned by MCP tool calls or listed by mcp_list_tools. Requires a configured, approved, reachable server; do not treat a resource URI as authorization.

mcp_tool.name: mcp_tool
mcp_tool.description: Unified tool for interacting with MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers. Available modes: 'list_servers' (lists all MCP servers you have access to), 'list_tools' (lists all tools and resources available on the specified MCP server), 'call_tool' (executes a specific tool on an MCP server with the provided JSON arguments), 'read_resource' (reads a specific resource from an MCP server).

server.description: Server name (required for list_tools, call_tool, read_resource).

tool_name.description: Name of the tool to execute (required for call_tool).

tool_args.description: JSON string containing the input arguments for the tool (optional for call_tool).

resource_uri.description: URI of the resource to read (required for read_resource).

shell_id.description: Optional custom shell ID for the command.

message_user.name: message_user
message_user.description: Send a message to the user. Optionally attach files by providing a list of absolute file paths or Opulent attachment URLs. Use this tool to send important updates to the user, respond to user questions, ask for clarification from the user, or report completion of a task. This is the only way to send messages to the user; the user will NOT see your normal messages unless you use this tool. You must u

message.description: The message to send to the user. Follow the communication style guidelines. Keep URLs intact - links are not counted as verbosity. Link evidence, attachments, recordings when helpful. Lead with any errors or issues.
