block_on_user.description: Whether to stop work and wait for a response from the user. Always set this field explicitly. Set to true when finished working or when blocked on the user. Set to false for progress updates, sharing deliverables like PR links, or any non-blocking status message.

attachments.description: Files to deliver to the user, as a list of absolute file paths (e.g. `/path/to/file.pdf`) or Opulent attachment URLs (e.g. `https://<webapp-host>/attachments/abc123/screenshot.png`). Always set this field explicitly: list every file your message references or promises (the user cannot access paths on your machine), or set it to an empty list [] when there is nothing to attach.

content_type.description: The type of message content. Defaults to 'text'. Use 'user_question' to present interactive choices.

questions.description: List of questions with options for the user to select from. Required when content_type is 'user_question'.

suggest_open_desktop.description: Optional flag to show the user a button that opens the Desktop tab in the webapp so they can watch and interact with your browser/desktop live. Set this when you want the user to try something running on your VM (a localhost server, a web UI, a game, etc.) — open it in your browser first, then set this flag so they can click one button to see it. Never send localhost URLs directly; the user cannot reach your VM's localhost but CAN see your desktop through this tab.

offer_to_test_app.description: Optional flag to offer the user the opportunity to have you test the app end-to-end. This will show a button to the user asking if they'd like you to test. Only set this when prompted by a system note after PR creation. When you do set this, include a one-liner in your message on what the testing would look like. If the user already approved or explicitly asked for testing, do not offer. When offering to test, the very last sentence should be an offer to record yourself testing, as to not lose the message. Ex. 'would you like me to record myself testing? Always provide `test_app_phrase` alongside this flag.

test_app_phrase.description: Only used when `offer_to_test_app` is true. A short imperative phrase describing what specifically would be tested, in roughly 25 characters or fewer. It is used as the label for the testing button shown to the user across interfaces, so make it context-aware rather than generic — e.g. "Test the webapp", "Run an eval", "Repro the bug". Falls back to "Test the app" when omitted.

user_action_required.description: Only used when `block_on_user` is true (ignored otherwise). A terse imperative phrase, ~20 chars or fewer, shown as a status label in the sessions sidebar (e.g. "Review PR", "Approve sessions"). If the user doesn't need to do anything, set this to exactly "None" — the sentinel for "no action", which the system suppresses. Don't use other wording like "N/A" or "None — informational".

message_workflow_agent.name: message_workflow_agent
message_workflow_agent.description: Send an message to a running dynamic-workflow agent (a local child session) without stopping the run. Use it to check on or steer an agent the soft-time-limit notification flagged.

run_id.description: The live run containing the agent.

agent_id.description: Agent result id reported by the soft-limit notification or get_workflow_output.

message.description: Message delivered to the agent as an interrupting system note. Omitted, a status check ("what are you doing, are you stuck?") is sent.

noop.name: noop
noop.description: Do nothing and return immediately. Call this only when no action is needed but you must emit a tool call. Never call it in place of an action, and never re-issue a tool call that already succeeded.

notebook_edit.name: notebook_edit
notebook_edit.description: Edit a cell in a Jupyter notebook file (.ipynb) - replace, insert, or delete cells

notebook_path.description: The absolute path to the Jupyter notebook file (.ipynb) to edit.

cell_number.description: The 0-based index of the cell to edit.

new_source.description: The new source content for the cell.

Read before making exact-string edits, and do not assume missing content means a file is empty when a limit was applied.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read.

offset.description: Optional line number to start reading from (1-based).

limit.description: Optional number of lines to read.

Do not assume an external completion notification is configured.

block.description: If true, block until the subagent finishes or the timeout expires.

timeout.description: Maximum number of seconds to wait when blocking. Defaults to 30, capped at 600, unless the tool description documents different limits for a specific subagent type.

recording_id.description: Optional recording ID. If not provided, one will be generated.

notify.description: Who should be notified: user, org_admin, or cognition.

severity.description: How urgent the fix is globally. Defaults to medium.

details.description: Markdown description of the blocker (expandable in UI).

recommended_action.description: What the notified party should do to resolve this.

tags.description: Freeform tags for Datadog faceting and trend analysis.

Skills provide context-specific g

suggest_save_secret.name: suggest_save_secret

suggest_skill_pr.name: suggest_skill_pr
suggest_skill_pr.description: Suggest creating or updating a SKILL.md file only for confirmed, reusable knowledge. Do not include secrets in plain text: reference a secret manager, and do not suggest unverified credentials or permission assumptions. Each SKILL.md should begin with YAML frontmatter containing name and description. Prefer improving an existing skill when appropriate. This creates a pending local suggestion, not an automatic pull request or hosted timeline card; a separately authorized approval flow is required for a PR.

task_create.name: task_create
task_create.description:
Create tasks on the session's structured task list. The list tracks your progress and gives the user visibility into what you are working on.

## When to use
Use tasks for multi-step work, non-trivial work that requires planning, when the user provides multiple tasks or explicitly asks for a task list, and to capture new requirements from the user as tasks immediately. Skip it for trivial, single-step, or purely conversational/informational requests — just do the work directly. Don't make single-task plans. Plan after reading the code, not before; tasks should name the concrete change, not generic phases (inspect, implement, test, commit).

## Task management
- Tasks start pending. Break complex work into specific, actionable tasks; create them together when planning.
- Use `task_update` to mark a task in_progress when starting it and completed IMMEDIATELY after finishing it. Keep exactly ONE task in_progress at a time.
- Add follow-up tasks discovered during work; use `task_update` with status "deleted" only for tasks genuinely no longer relevant or created in error.
- Use `task_list` to check the current list before adding tasks so you don't create duplicates.

## Example
For "Add a dark mode toggle to settings, then run tests and build", create tasks:
1. subject: "Add dark mode toggle component to settings page", active_form: "Adding dark mode toggle component"
2. subject: "Wire up dark mode state management"
3. subject: "Update existing components to support theme switching"
4. subject: "Run tests and build, fixing any failures"

subject.description: A brief title in imperative form (e.g. "Fix authentication bug", "Run tests and build").

description.description: Detailed context: requirements, acceptance criteria, relevant files, and the planned approach.

active_form.description: Present-continuous form shown while the task is in progress (e.g. "Fixing authentication bug").

task_get.name: task_get
task_get.description: Get the full details of a single task by ID, including its description and dependencies (blocks / blocked_by).

task_id.description: The ID of the task to fetch.

task_list.name: task_list
task_list.description: List all tasks on the session's task list with their IDs, statuses, and unresolved blockers. Use it to review progress, find the next task to work on, and avoid creating duplicate tasks.

task_update.name: task_update
task_update.description:
Update tasks on the session's task list by ID: change status, edit fields, record dependencies, or delete.

## Status flow
- Mark a task in_progress when beginning work on it. Keep exactly ONE task in_progress at a time.
- Mark a task completed IMMEDIATELY after fully finishing it.
- ONLY mark a task completed when it is fully done — not when tests are failing, the implementation is partial, or errors are unresolved. If you hit a blocker, keep the task in_progress and create a new task describing what must be resolved.
- Never silently drop user-requested tasks: if one seems infeasible, keep it in_progress or blocked and message the user (non-blocking) with what you tried and what's blocking you — the user may have context you lack. Use status "deleted" only for tasks that are genuinely no longer relevant or were created in error.
- Use add_blocks / add_blocked_by to record ordering dependencies between tasks.

task_id.description: The ID of the task to update.

status.description: New status. Use "deleted" to remove a task created in error or no longer relevant.

active_form.description: New present-continuous form shown while in progress.

add_blocked_by.description: Task IDs that block this task (added to any existing ones).

add_blocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks (added to any existing ones).

testing_agent.name: testing_agent
testing_agent.description: Hand off UI-driven testing to a local child agent; do not use it for shell-verifiable tests, lint, type checks or builds. The first handoff requires `user_testing_request` approval evidence. Subsequent handoffs message the existing child and return its agent_id/status; call `read_subagent` to wait for or inspect its result. Do not claim a recording or verdict until the returned evidence exists. Child capabilities and credentials depend on runtime configuration; never assume access to a provider or secret.

message.description: A message to the testing agent. State what to test, the behaviors or acceptance criteria to verify, and any relevant setup or environment changes.

user_testing_request.description: The testing approval evidence: the sentence from the user's message that requests or approves this testing, quoted verbatim. Required on the first handoff.

todo_write.name: todo_write
todo_write.description: Use this tool to create and manage a structured task list for your current session. It tracks your progress and gives the user visibility into what you are working on.

todos.description: The updated list of todo items.

status.description: Current status of the todo item.

query.description: A natural language query describing the task or desired tool capability. This input is passed through tokenization, stemming, and stopword removal, so keep it focused and keyword-rich rather than writing a full sentence.

limit.description: Maximum number of ranked tools to return. Use lower values for a focused result or higher values to explore the catalog. Default value is 10.

upload_attachment.name: upload_attachment
upload_attachment.description: Upload a workspace file to configured artifact storage and get a `storage://` pointer, not a public URL. Use it when an artifact pointer is needed elsewhere; pass workspace paths to `message_user` attachments to share files with the user. Multiple `file_paths` are supported. Requires the configured storage repository and branch; do not claim a public download URL.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file on the box to upload. The file will be uploaded to cloud storage and a URL will be returned.

file_paths.description: A list of absolute file paths on the box to upload. Use this instead of file_path when uploading multiple files at once.

view_image.name: view_image
view_image.description: View a local image file from the filesystem. Use this only when you are given or already know the full file path and the image is not already in context. The path must resolve within the configured workspace. This returns encoded image data from a local file; remote URLs need a separate authenticated provider.

wait.name: wait
wait.description: Wait for a non-event-driven delay using positive `seconds` and a concise `message`. Use this only when there is no better completion signal; do not add delays between your own tool calls or wait for user replies. Prefer `get_output` for background shell processes and a provider-specific status check for CI or external jobs. The handler caps the actual delay at 600 seconds and can be aborted by the current run; it does not itself subscribe to external notifications.

seconds.description: Number of seconds to wait. Must be positive. Values above 600 are clamped to 600.

message.description: A concise explanation (no more than 10 words) of why the wait is needed.

web_get_contents.name: web_get_contents
web_get_contents.description: Fetch the text contents of one or more web pages by URL. Use this when you need to read the full text of a specific web page or extract content from multiple URLs at once (max 10). Use it after `web_search` to read promising public results. Only public HTTP(S) text/HTML/JSON on standard ports is accepted; private IPs, oversized content, and credential-bearing URLs are rejected.

urls.description: List of URLs to fetch content from (max 10).

web_search.name: web_search
web_search.description:
Search the web for information using a search query. Returns relevant web page titles, URLs, and summaries. Use this when you need to find information online.

You must not include extraneous information in web searches. For example, to find latest python version, do *NOT* search "latest Python version 2026 3.11 3.12 3.13". The "2026 3.11 3.12 3.13" is unnecessary. Keep the search string simple and focused, e.g. "latest Python version".

query.description: The search query to find relevant web pages. Keep the search string simple and focused.

num_results.description: Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 5.

domain.description: Optional domain to restrict search results to (e.g. 'docs.rs').

write.name: write
write.description:
Write content to a file inside the configured sandbox workspace, creating it if needed and overwriting it if it exists.

Usage:
- Prefer the edit tool for modifying existing files. Only use this tool to create new files or for complete rewrites.
- If overwriting an existing file, you SHOULD use the read tool first to read the file's contents.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files unless explicitly requested.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write

content.description: The content to write to the file

write_to_process.name: write_to_process
write_to_process.description: Write to a still-running interactive process identified by `shell_id`; if no process is running, use `exec` instead. Provide exactly one of `text_input` or `bytes_input`. `text_input` is literal text. `bytes_input` recognizes `<ENTER>`, `<RETURN>`, `<TAB>`, `<ESC>`, `<CTRL_C>`, `<CTRL_D>`, and `<BACKSPACE>`; other angle-bracket tokens are sent literally. Check the process result and avoid sending secrets in tool arguments.

shell_id.description: The ID of the shell to write to.

text_input.description: Text content to write to the shell (interpreted as literal text).

bytes_input.description: Special characters/bytes to write to the shell (interpreted with angle bracket notation).
